plan.title: UC colon GSVA hallmark pathway scoring & heatmap
plan.analytical_narrative: The research question asks for a per-sample pathway activity score and a heatmap of hallmark activity separating UC-inflamed from control colon samples (6 vs 6, unpaired, single batch, raw Salmon gene counts, 12000 genes). The standard route to a per-sample score (rather than a single group-level enrichment p-value) is GSVA on variance-stabilized expression, tested afterward with limma against the same design used for differential expression. Before that, the raw counts need a standard DESeq2 QC + DE pass: sample-structure QC (flagging sample_01's low library size per the caveat, keeping it unless QC shows it is an outlier), minimal low-count filtering, DESeq2 normalization, Wald test with apeglm shrinkage, and BH-FDR — this both answers the DE side and produces the vst-transformed matrix GSVA needs. GSVA then scores every sample against the MSigDB Hallmark human gene set collection staged in the reference store, one score per sample per hallmark, and limma tests each hallmark score between UC-inflamed and control. The final step renders the heatmap (samples x hallmarks, annotated by condition and by library-size flag) and assembles the report with all required reproducibility fields (versions, thresholds, gene set collection version, session info).

steps.method: vst(blind) + PCA + sample distance heatmap + library size QC
keep genes with >=10 counts in >= smallest group size (6)
GSVA per-sample pathway scores (Hallmark, Poisson kernel on counts/gaussian on vst) then limma on scores for group comparison; heatmap of scores
Integrated report with QC, DE results, GSVA heatmap, session info
